channel.title: Muhammad Jahanzaib Awan — Writing
channel.description: Short technical posts on machine learning, evaluation and data science.

item.title: Data Leakage in Time Series: Lag Features Need Care
item.description: Lag features feel safe because they look backwards, but sloppy construction lets future information leak in and inflates your validation scores.

item.title: Hyperparameter Search: Grid, Random, and Bayesian, Honestly
item.description: Grid search is comfortable, random search is underrated, and Bayesian optimisation earns its complexity only sometimes. Here is the honest comparison.

item.title: Explaining Transformers Without the Film Analogy Trap
item.description: Skip the film analogies. Here is how to explain transformers to non-technical people using a concrete weighted-vote example that actually holds up.

item.title: What a Model Evaluation Framework Automates and Assumes
item.description: Evaluation frameworks automate splitting, scoring, and aggregation, but they quietly assume your data is independent, your split reflects deployment, and your metric means what you think.

item.title: How to Shortlist MLOps Tools Without Chasing Every Release
item.description: A practical filter for choosing MLOps tools on a small team, so you stop re-evaluating your stack every time something new trends.

item.title: Data Science Salary Bands Explained by Skill
item.description: Salary bands in data science track judgement under uncertainty, not tool familiarity. Here is the skill ladder that actually explains the pay gap.

item.title: Building a Personal MLOps Toolkit Before Paying for a Platform
item.description: Managed MLOps platforms solve real problems, but most of those problems can be handled first with free tools, discipline, and a bit of scripting.

item.title: Why Extreme Risk Evaluation Needs More Than a Test Set
item.description: Held-out accuracy answers a narrow question. For rare, high-consequence failures, you need adversarial probing, distribution shift tests, and honest uncertainty, not just a leaderboard score.

item.title: Evaluation Metrics: Interview Talk vs What You Actually Compute
item.description: Interviews want clean definitions of precision, recall and AUC. Real projects want you to know which one lies to you and when.

item.title: The Gap Between a Data Science Internship Advert and the Job
item.description: The advert promises neural networks and predictive models. The job mostly delivers spreadsheets, missing values, and meetings about definitions.

item.title: Choosing a Data Science Degree: What Maps to Real Work
item.description: Module lists promise a lot. Here is how to tell which ones actually build the skills data science jobs use every day.

item.title: Why 'Transformer' Means Something Different in ML Papers
item.description: In electrical engineering a transformer changes voltage. In machine learning it changes how a model attends to context. Same word, unrelated ideas.

item.title: A Realistic Weekly Breakdown of MLOps Work
item.description: Model training is the smallest part of the job. Here is the honest weekly rhythm of maintaining ML systems in production.

item.title: When Evaluation Dashboards Hide Silent Model Failures
item.description: A clean accuracy chart on a managed ML dashboard can hide leakage, drift, and slice-level failures that only careful, manual evaluation will reveal.

item.title: Reading an MLOps Certification Syllabus: Gaps and Gains
item.description: MLOps syllabuses teach you the pipeline plumbing well, but often skip the harder judgement calls around evaluation, drift, and leakage.

item.title: Bootcamps vs Self-Taught Paths: What Portfolios Reveal
item.description: Bootcamp or self-taught, the credential says little. The portfolio, read carefully, says almost everything about how someone actually thinks.

item.title: How to Read an Evaluation Section Like a Reviewer
item.description: Skip the leaderboard instinct. Learn to interrogate splits, baselines, and variance the way a careful reviewer does, not the way a skimmer does.

item.title: Knowledge Distillation: Shrinking a Model Without Breaking It
item.description: Distillation can quietly shrink a model's failure modes into a smaller package. Here's how to check whether you've actually preserved behaviour, not just accuracy.

item.title: Multi-Task Learning: When a Shared Backbone Helps or Hurts
item.description: A shared backbone sounds efficient, but it only pays off when tasks actually agree on what a good representation looks like.

item.title: Warm Restarts and Why a Constant Learning Rate Rarely Wins
item.description: A constant learning rate forces a single compromise between speed and stability. Schedules, especially warm restarts, let you have both at different points in training.
